Since the project and its inhabitants constitute a good representative cross section of the City, the ensuing discussion, in most instances, relates to both the City and project, e.g., general economic data, employment, the climate, etc.
a. Location
Some general information of this topic has previously been given in this report. In further discussion of its location, it might be noted that the City is situated 115 miles north of Washington, D.C., 105 miles west of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and 170 miles southwest of New York City. (See Regional Location, Appendix D)
b. Population
Harrisburg is the seventh largest city in the Commonwealth. In 1970, the population of the City was 68,061 (U.S. Census, 1970). Since 1950, the population of Harrisburg has been declining. The surrounding townships, however, have shown marked population increases, chiefly in areas peripheral to the City. One, for example, Lower Paxton Township, almost tripled in population from 1950 to 1960, and again increased by over 50 percent in the decade ending 1970.
The following population data (Table 1) is given for a comparison between the City and other demographic areas within the region. Figures for 1980 are also projected in the Table. Immediately following Table 1, Table 2, provides a good breakdown of the City's population by age distribution.
c. Topography
The area surrounding Harrisburg is generally rolling farm country typical of southeastern Pennsylvania. The City's elevation above mean sea level is approximately 310 feet. The relief of the City is not particularly severe. The project area likewise has very little noticeable relief.
d. Soil
Basically, a large portion of the City, including the business and governmental centers, are located on the soil association known as the Duncannon-Chevies-Tioga (D-C-T) Associations.
